Binance US said the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has deemed its applications to register as a designated contract market (DCM) and derivatives clearing organization (DCO) substantially complete, moving them into substantive review. Neither application has been approved. DCM registration would allow Binance US to offer derivatives trading, including futures and options, while DCO registration would allow it to clear those trades. Binance US plans to use both registrations to offer U.S. users regulated derivatives, including perpetual futures. It has not launched any derivatives products and must await formal CFTC approval before doing so.

According to the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) website, BAM Derivatives LLC submitted Binance US’s application to register as a designated contract market (DCM). Even if investors expect eventual bailouts to drive prices higher, they may still need cash now to avoid liquidation in less liquid positions.
